title: Bugs in Evernote
body:
Ever know has been going downhill rapidly over the last few weeks or months. It’s almost unusable on my phone at this point and it’s so slow and filled with bugs on the laptop that we’re ready to give up and shift to GROK4.7 and shift to using agents to manage the things we previously managed on Evernote and are now having to give up and just consider it our archive 

I understand you’ve bundled some type of integration with hugging face or something like that, but you need to get your code debug before you go live with it. This is very concerning that your company is letting down it users this way after all these years 

What is tell me about Evernote having use it for over a decade now this is dedication to being a Bake with respect to communication with his customers which would help in its product development

body:

title: These constant changes are not helpful.
body:
I’ve been using Evernote since around 2010. It’s had improvements over the years. Been bought and sold by different owners. Changes made. Price has gone up as has the price for everything else. Features come. Features go.

This year the price went from $150 a year to $260 a year. This for a bunch of features that were already deployed for the most part and that I hadn’t used quite frankly. Obviously, I’m invested in the technology since I’ve used it for 16 years. Not anxious to have to move everything to some other platform.

This week, I used Evernote to file photos that I took during a competitive review of our businesses. When I went back in to review the photos their “helpful” AI has not inserted an annoying AI assessment of what is in each image. 

Additionally, I use Evernote to house lyrics and charts for a music project that I play in. This week, all of the charts had been kicked down approximately 50 spaces on the page which required me to go in and edit every note to bring them back up to the top of the note - DURING THE PERFORMANCE. Super frustrating.

Obviously their testing criteria doesn’t involve user feedback.

title: Was a favorite app, $250 a year now? LOL
body:
Price jump from $99 to $250 a year. After 12+ years of using Evernote, I'm done. A ridiculous price increase of 250%. Move my hundreds of notes into the Apple Notes app.


Added a new note, ended up with 13 duplicate copies. What a joke.

So, I accessed a note, and added some info. That note now shows up 9 times in the far left column. Why? So, I now have one recipe in 9 separate notes. It saved each time I backspaced to correct my typing. I don't need 9 notes for one recipe. This is a huge bug. This update is horrible.

Ok, so you must use the EDIT button to edit a note. If you don't, you get multiple duplicates. Why can the keyboard be invoked for typing without using the Edit button? Lose that Edit Button.

September 2020 update is horrible. Why can't you view Notebooks on the left side in a column? Now to see them, it takes the entire page, and there is no threaded view of notes within their Notebook. Who designed this new interface? It's awful.

Evernote has become almost useless. It is slow, it locks up when trying to select text, it's difficult to find notes, everything that made this app so great seems to have been removed or changed.

No full view for notes in iOS? When I'm using Slide Over on my iPad Pro, once I find the note I need, I don't need the left side pane to stay up. I want to see the whole note. 

When trying to copy text, the menu comes up for Select and Select All...but this freezes the app, every time. The only way to unfreeze it is to use the Home button and swipe the app up to close it. Then the next time I open that note, no changes were kept.

I'm looking for something else to use. This app has been ruined, not to mention the ridiculous price increase for what should be normal features.

title: Used to love this app until they eliminated my plan

title: Evernote Made Me Hate Evernote
body:
I used Evernote for 10–12 years and spent about eight of those meaning to find a better alternative.
Disclaimer: I always used the free plan, so yes, I’m complaining about a free service. But Evernote’s longstanding two-device limit never made upgrading feel like a value-add. It felt like ransom for the privilege of accessing my own notes across devices like it isn’t 2012.
I didn’t use it heavily: maybe 150 notes across 10 notebooks—recipes, clothing sizes, part numbers, quotations, and other small things I wanted to keep. I mostly treated it as a notebook that lived on my phone.
Today I opened Evernote to find a recipe and discovered the free tier had become dramatically more restrictive—roughly one notebook and 50 notes. I couldn’t even properly access my existing collection without accepting a seven-day trial that would begin billing about $250 per year.
So I spent the morning screenshotting notes, copying and pasting them elsewhere, and occasionally exporting them in Evernote’s proprietary format. Then I canceled the trial and deleted the app.
I will happily pay for Notion or Obsidian Sync. I will not give money to a company that uses access to my existing notes as leverage.

Congratulations, Evernote: you freed up about 5 MB of storage today. A small part of me hopes that same 5 MB eventually stores your Chapter 11 filing.

Two significant frustrations are:

1. It doesn’t give you an opportunity to return to the same place. You leave your note for an hour, you end up at the front door. Frustrating if you’re trying to get work done!

2. Formatting is picky, idiosyncratic, and doesn’t play well with mail. Bullets and numbering are particularly frustrating because most of the time bullets work just fine. Other times you copy from Evernote and paste into mail (or other apps) and one bullet is different and can’t be fixed unless you redo formatting for the entire message. (Convert to text then reformat everything by hand. )

So is it useful? Yes. Was it worth the previous, smaller subscription? Yeah.

title: iOS version almost unusable
body:
I’ve been a loyal Evernote user for 10+ years and ~18k notes.

It seems that there is a significant subset of users for whom the iOS app is extremely slow, losing text just entered, causing multiple conflicting versions of notes, and getting “stuck” where pressing the green check mark doesn’t save the note and change to the back arrow (<). I’m one of those.

(The fix is to delete and reinstall the Evernote iOS app. But the fix lasts only a few days and must be repeated.)

These issues have been discussed for the past few years on various forums.

It also seems that not everyone has these issues. For the majority of users, Evernote iOS seems to be working fine.

So, this subset of utterly frustrated users is very disappointed with Evernote management for rolling out new (fairly minor) features, and not fixing core issues of basic functionality.

There are many of us who have reluctantly switched from Evernote to another service. Most of those have probably done that without writing anything in a review or forum. I’m about to be one of those defectors.

To those of you for whom Evernote iOS works fine, I wish you well. Hopefully this explains the one-star reviews.

title: Watch out! They’ll hold your data hostage!
body:
I was a loyal Evernote user for years. I paid for premium, built my entire note system in it, and trusted the platform with a significant amount of personal and professional data.

I eventually moved to Microsoft OneNote because it’s more affordable and, frankly, has surpassed Evernote in both usability and value.

Coming back now to retrieve my data has been a frustrating and disappointing experience. Features that used to be standard are now locked behind aggressive limitations. The web app refuses access due to notebook limits. Device restrictions prevent normal syncing. The overall experience feels intentionally designed to make it difficult to leave without paying again.

Call it what you want, but from a user perspective it feels like my own data is being held behind artificial barriers.

I understand companies need to monetize, but there’s a difference between charging for features and creating friction around data access. This approach erodes trust and punishes long-time users who simply want to move on.

I would strongly recommend that anyone considering Evernote think carefully about long-term data ownership and exit costs. Getting your information in is easy. Getting it out is another story.

title: pros might not outweigh the cons
body:
TLDR Summary: it probably isn't worth the hefty price tag. 

Cons:
-The price has doubled twice in three years. $21/month is what you'll have to pay to sync your notes on your phone, iPad, laptop and work desktop. If you can get by with three devices, you might be able to squeak by on the Starter plan.
- One of the new "updates" by promoted by the developer is a new pricing plan. What a spin! You're telling me that one of the new "features" I have to pay for is a more expensive pricing structure?
-Another new feature is the AI inclusion, meaning that machine learning will be used to read and sort your information. Only on the Enterprise plan is ownership of data guaranteed; check the privacy policy for how they determine ownership of what you upload. What you upload will be shared with OpenAi and other unnamed third parties, meaning that those audio files will share what your voice sounds like with an undisclosed third party. 
-In the phone app, you can export or download a note as a psf file. The only way to share is via a link or email.

Pros:
-The Web Clipper browser extension. I've found it incredibly useful to be able to save pages and paragraphs from websites.
-Scannable. The ability to convert image-to-text or image-to-pdf has been helpful, although it's a bummer the Scannable app costs extra.
-Handwritting recognition? I don't use handwriting features often, but I like the idea of converting ink to digital format (replacing all of the Rocketbooks and smart notebooks I've tried with a regular old pen & paper). 

Neutral: Some features are a given with any note-taking app and I'm listing them here so it's clear why they don't help a consumer choose Evernote:
-Tags to sort your content 
-Notebooks to organize by subject (Only 20 if you're using the Starter plan)
-Templates
-Calendar integration (but tbh this is done better by the apps with strong email integration like Microsoft OneNote or Google imho)

I was notified of a change in pricing and automatically signed up for their new premium service.  I changed the option to what I thought was the version I was currently in for ~ $20/year.  Next thing that happens is that I am “at my limit” for notebooks (by no means do I have very many, in fact they can all be displayed on 1 screen…) and would need to subscribe to the several hundred dollar version to add more notebooks.  Also now it keeps blocking me from accessing my info saying it can only be accessed on “3 devices”.  I have an iPhone, iPad, desktop and they count their website as one.  They also limit you from making changes to approved devices.  So my Evernote subscription is now pretty worthless……after paying them their $20 for the next 12 months.  Now have to go through the trouble of offloading my info and find a new product.

title: Great. Not perfect, but great
body:

I don’t think any other notes app I’ve used comes close. I’ll be using Evernote forever. 
And, the more you use it, the more useful it becomes, as in having important papers (credentials for me) at the reach of your phone.
MY FAVORITE new improvement is with the camera/scanning function. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you for making the “business card” an option instead of auto-sensing. The entire camera/scanning function feels new and improved, so I changed my long-ago review from a four-star to a five-star review. 
Great app. 
Well worth the cost, both the free and paid (which I gladly pay each year) versions. I probably don’t even use a quarter of Evernote’s full potential. I love it. 
I use it almost every day.

title: Excellent product
body:
I’ve been using Evernote for about 13 years. I use it mainly to store information, jot down thoughts, plan errands. I like how they’re constantly improving features, especially the Headings feature so my notes can look organized with headings and sub-headings.  Can’t imagine how my life would’ve been without it. Love the product!

For improvement, I’d love to see a navigation pane (as seen on MS Word) on the left side of the note so I can quickly navigate to sections. My notes are often long with multiple sections assigned to their respective headings. Currently, I’m having to scroll all the way up to the top of the note to be able to navigate to the desired sections because that’s where I put the Table of Content. It would be nice to have a nav pane that’s always present on the left of the note.

title: Feeling increasingly trapped
body:
I’ve been a Loyal Customer for years, and so I have close to 4,000 notes…but it seems around every corner Evernote raises their price without any lower tiers for those who just want to keep their data but don’t want all the extra stuff.

If you use it like a general note application you'll never "get" all the hype about Evernote. 

The reason I know this is because that's what I never understood. 

I never understood why I heard so many business people raving about Evernote until I finally learned this: you have to jump in headfirst and put your ENTIRE LIFE into the application. 

When you do it will radically change everything. 

I categorize everything. Creative Ideas, expenses, projects, quotes, articles, my coaching notes for my son’s football team, vacations info, trip planning, home remodeling projects, notes for business meetings, etc.

title: Great job!!
body:
Evernote’s latest update, especially the new AI features, is a significant improvement.
The built-in AI Assistant feels like a smart helper in my notes, ready to find, organize, or expand on ideas effortlessly. I can ask it questions in plain language, and it understands my meaning, not just the exact words.
Search has become smarter. Typing “that meeting where we planned the Q3 roadmap” retrieves the correct notes instead of random keyword matches, simplifying the retrieval of old projects and ideas.
The AI that handles meeting notes is a game changer. It summarizes long conversations into clear summaries with key points and action items, so I don’t have to write everything down. I can easily share a clean recap with my team afterward.
I love how AI cleans up messy notes, fixing typos, adding structure, and even rewriting them into emails or bullet points. It saves me a lot of time spent editing.
This Evernote version feels genuine, not just AI-tacked on. It simplifies my daily work and keeps me organized with less effort. For note-obsessed users, this update is worth using.

title: Time to put this elephant out of its misery
body:
I don’t think any of the previous versions issues have been resolved but for some reason Evernote has been rewritten from the ground up with the best features slowly being added back. 

——

Evernote is my go to note taking app. I like being able to take a screen clipping, add some notes, set a reminder. Past that, it’s really fallen behind on the times. 

It’s just not very good at taking notes. Every little aspect of the note taking process is limited or tedious. 

It’s time for there to be live/instant as you type saving of notes. 

Also, sharing is a joke. No collaboration. No commenting. 

Annotations haven’t been updated in years and are basically useless on images and somewhat helpful on PDF’s. 

It has some of the worst outline note taking features out there. 

Lastly, it’s time to be able to record a meeting and have time synced notes that other users can comment and/or collaborate on. 

Seriously, sharing is useless.

So why do I still use it?  Scan, clip or photo anything and everything and all the text in those images becomes searchable making it super easy to use Evernote as a big file dumpster and add a reminder to that note and you may not forget to renew your car registration.

Evernote has been particularly valuable and useful in recovering from a devastating house fire in which EVERYTHING was lost save what we were wearing or carrying.  My iPhone survived because I was communicating with 911, so its access to my Evernote and other online services were essential for access to scanned and saved data to aid the recovery processes. 

The ability to readily share information through granting access to specific Evernote folders to insurance and attorney personnel has been spectacularly helpful. None had previously been aware of Evernote, and all were delighted by the ease and convenience provided by Evernote for sharing essential information and documentation. 

The greater functionalities now available in the browser version of Evernote is most welcome because I use it much more now that I am back to using two Linux Mint computers. (The Windows version of Evernote is truly excellent, but in recent years, I have found Windows to be too annoying because of incessant efforts by Windows trying to force me to use their preferred products rather than the ones that I prefer. I used it to compile school notes, work drafts, story outlines, and whatever else I needed a page for. 

I thoroughly enjoyed being able to jump from my computer to my phone with no worries of sync delays and was able to pickup right where I left off.

However, since it became a premium feature to have more than one device on an account I found my enjoyment and usage have rapidly declined.

Not to mention the free plan now only lets you have 1 Notebook and only 50 notes, which I maxed out when this became a feature instantaneously, having surpassed 50 notes forever ago. I had to downsize greatly to write more before I first bought premium, which I didn’t pay for long as I don’t use a ton of the more professional or advanced features.

It is limiting and pushed me to look for other apps for my notes but nothing I found was able to meet the expectations of what Evernote previously met for me.

If the free version of Evernote allowed for 2 devices, 2 notebooks, and at minimum 100 notes I’d be a lot happier. 

I do not use Evernote for work or school anymore, just personal writings and outlines that I use as a means to relax and unwind, though recently it’s become more of a headache than I care to deal with and find myself using my phone’s note app again.

I greatly miss what Evernote was.

title: Love the new features, and it’s running much better
body:
December 2025 I’m having trouble getting it to open linked notes that I haven’t recently opened. Ditto for using Command + J to pull up note names. Thank god for back links and Search, otherwise I’d have trouble finding and opening many of my notes. 

—-xxx—- 

I’m also frustrated with the Transcribe function, which sometimes works perfectly and sometimes simply invents things. I transcribed a couple of really clear photos of product packages a few days ago. One was transcribed faithfully word for word, bit the other was not. Evernote didn’t transcribe anything that was written bit instead made up its own riff on the contents, like a high school sophomore writing a book report. It seems to me the transcribe feature has degraded, at least for phots. I really relied on it. 

—-xxx—-

August 2025 The program is running much more smoothly now. I still wish that headers functioned a bit differently, which I get into below. —- xxx —- I love the transcription feature. So far I’ve only tested this with pictures and screenshots (I think it also works with audio) and it’s fantastic. I’m always capturing recipes, and I like to rewrite and work with them to suit me. Previously I would tediously type them out by hand, but now I no longer need to. —-xxx—- Regarding Headers: I only wish for a few improvements in these: - That you could use headers within tables, as I like the visual formatting of having most of the content of my notes within tables, and it would be nice to be able to create expandable / collapsible sections within these, as I don’t always want to see everything at once. Collapsible sections would make for easier scrolling as well. … - … I wish notes did not “update” every time you expand or collapse a header section. These are not true updates, and it confuses me and wastes time when scrolling through recently updated notes to find something. It also causes problems when searching a note’s history to look at changes and deletions, as it causes empty “updates” to appear when there have been no actual changes. …. Another time waster when I’m trying to find something. - It ‘s great that when searching inside a note the search function includes the content of any headers. What’s not great is that searching expands any headers with content that matches, and then leaves these expanded, requiring me to manually collapse them, one by one. This is a real pain. Also, and again, this expansion causes the note to “update.” …-… I wish headers automatically collapsed when you navigate away from a note. I hate re-opening notes and having to collapse a bunch of lengthy headers before I can reach the note content. It would be cool if maybe they were like a menu whose contents appeared when your mouse hovers over the title, and whose contents you could click on, but which did not actually expand. …-… That leads me into my final wish for headers, that they could be used like on website pages where, for say all the notes in a notebook, or perhaps all of a group of notes you selected, headers would automatically populate from a main / control page, and any changes you made to that main page’s headers would push through to all the other notes in that group. Regarding other things I brought up in my original review, I still have not figured out the table of contents thing, and I’m still looking for an easier way to search on iOs. —- ORIGINAL REVIEW—- There is still nothing near as good as Evernote to replace it with. I thought about doing so repeatedly during recent years, but there’s nothing that combines the functionality of web clipping, notebooks, tags, links to other notes, PDF attachments/annotations/searching, etc. all with pretty much instant updating across multiple devices. I use it nearly much every minute of the day, far more than any other software or application. I store everything in it except for passwords and other highly sensitive information. For those things I use 1Password and have been experimenting with Proton Pass. Some of the newer features the Evernote team has added, such as using the slash command (/) to bring up a whole menu of items you can add to notes, are pretty cool. The best of these, for me, is that you can add a link to a note without navigating to that note and copying the link, as long as you can remember more or less the title of it. As soon as you start typing words from that note title, a list of all notes containing those words appear, and you may then select the one whose link you want to copy and paste. That is so helpful. Saves me tons of time trying for find and organize information. Wishlist - I do wish the slash-command menu worked within tables, which are what I use to organize notes generally. So far, these only work in the main body of the note, outside of any tables you created. - Headers are a helpful feature, as is the new ability to expand and collapse menu items under these, but again, this doesn’t work within tables, which is a bummer. Also, it seems to me I saw an announcement recently after an update about some features I haven’t been able to find or work with so far. Perhaps these are Windows-only at the moment? I was very excited to see an announcement about being able to create tables of contents within notes for easier navigation within them. That is something I have wanted for a looong time and have created many workarounds that work far better on a computer upon which I can easily hit Command + F to find the section I am looking for, than on mobile, where search is pretty tedious.

title: Don’t know what I would do without Evernote!
body:
I have used Evernote for about 15 years for a huge variety of things and I LOVE it! 

Anytime I read an interesting article and I don’t want to lose it - Evernote it!  In fact that should be a verb just like googling :)

I love that I don’t have to take the time to figure out where it should go. I can quickly tag it and easily find it by the amazing search functionality of Evernote.

Every year I have a thoughts log that serves as my journal or diary - and my self-therapy.  I can wail all I want in a note which usually frees me up to have a constructive day.

I keep my daily personal task list in Evernote.  And I’ll do more specific task lists - like packing for a trip.

When I have been looking for a piece of furniture, I’ll save photos or online shopping ideas to an Evernote file with my thoughts about those options.  It helps me think through what I want.

When I am doing my taxes, even though I have files in google or on my hard drive, I find it much easier to document remaining questions that I am trying to resolve in Evernote.

I also keep my want to see movies, want to read books, etc in Evernote.  In theory those could be in google files, but it’s just so much easier in Evernote!  I am on the NYC subway a lot and Evernote syncs so easily as we come in and out of stations with WIFI.

title: Congratulations Evernote you’ve chased me away

I’ve been using Evernote for well over 10 years.

At the beginning, the license model was purchase and use. There weren’t any monthly plans. When they started pushing the monthly plans, I simplified my notes experience and changed my strategy because clearly it wasn’t going to be a cost-effective manner to track many notes.

For the next 10+ years, I would login periodically to access and sometimes update notes that I used on a regular basis. Example, I kept the gift list for my wife. Eventually, it became so painful to use the app because of pop-ups that I’m now not even using it for that anymore. Was tagging and checklist and some of the Evernote features nice to have? Sure, they were useful for when I would have a gift idea and then check it off as having given it to my wife. But not worth the ridiculous monthly plans that Evernote is forcing down my throat each time I go to access that note. Every time my wife says she has a gift idea, I cringe. Not because I have a gift to buy, I’m happy to do that. But because I have to access Evernote and click through constant pop-ups to get to a simple text note that lists the gift ideas I have for the woman I love.

In summary, you’ve made what should be a simple experience, incredibly inconvenient and annoying.

title: My favorite app.
body:
Evernote has changed the way I catalog information. It's a new kind of database, which goes far beyond the tabular formats of spreadsheets or conventional databases like MS Access. Arrange data into notebooks and custom-sort notes from different notebooks by assigning a TAG to them when they're related in some way. Make notes with any combination of pictures, voice or other sound records, text, and virtually any kind of file. Multiple-media notes will likely restore an "emotional" element so you can recall them. Writers, speakers, comedians, and musicians, whose careers may depend upon flash-bulb types of ideas, may find Evernote indispensable. 

Install Evernote onto several devices and they stay in sync automatically via the "cloud."

Find notes by browsing notebooks or TAGs. Sort them to isolate the ones with sound recordings. Search by keyword (which can be in note titles, notebook names, TAGs, or text), and find them that way. Evernote can even find handwritten words in pictures. And if you knew you recorded a great note but cannot remember the first thing about it, search for it by location, since Evernote can geotag every note you make. 

I use Evernote for all kinds of things. As a drummer, I often cannot transcribe rhythm ideas before they escape my imagination. But with Evernote, I can open a new note, put my device on the table, tap the rhythm out with my hands and feet, and speak my thought process at the time. Location and time of day may help me remember how I felt just then and restore any of the, well, MEANING behind the idea. 

For those who have shutdown problems, keeping all devices up to date with the latest versions may help. Uninstalling and reinstalling the app is easy and often fixes the problem.

title: FIX MAC CURSOR ISSUE
body:
I am a new Evernote user, but the current Mac app (v10+) has become completely unusable for serious note-taking due to a persistent and infuriating **cursor bug**. When typing, the cursor jumps to previous positions, completely ignoring where I am actually typing. This happens even in small notes, but is especially severe in notes with images or formatting.  

I have tried restarting the app, splitting notes, reinstalling, and turning off syncing—none of these reliably fix the issue. The app’s lack of control over cache, formatting, and text handling makes it impossible to work efficiently. For professionals who rely on Evernote for research, writing, or any serious work, this is a critical failure.  

This is not a minor annoyance—it is a **major bug that effectively breaks typing in the app**. It needs immediate attention from Evernote’s developers. Users should not have to workaround basic functionality like cursor placement in a paid productivity app.  

Please fix this immediately. This issue is making Evernote effectively unusable, and continued neglect risks losing your user base entirely.

title: Dramatic Improvementbover last 12 months

I really wish they would publicly explain how they keep our information safe from cyber threats, but I’m hanging in there as a paid subscriber and am hopeful of continued improvement in all areas, including security.   That said, no other notes-focused information management platform has the mix of features, capabilities and ease of use that EN has, and I really mean that. title: I love love love Evernote!
body:
love love love Evernote! I have been using it for several years … for both personal and business purposes (mostly personal). I use it to keep track of personal information, shopping lists, to-do lists, checklists, capturing my favorite YouTube videos, reminders, expenses, Christmas shopping lists, to track which gifts I have ordered, received, wrapped, and delivered, etc.


Some of my favorite features are:
- Seamless access across multiple devices and platforms.
- The ability to share notes with Evernote users … and NON-USERS alike.
- The personal email address that allows me to email things into my notes library.
- Its AI automation (especially with Alexa) via IFTTT.
- The ability to save YouTube videos and information from the Internet via clipping.
- The ability to create notes via typing or dictation.
- The ability to create notes with words, audio, video, photos, attachments, etc.
- The generous storage limits (I have over 3,000 notes in my library!).


This tool is easy to use. It is extremely user-friendly for beginners … but very robust with tons of functionality for those who wish to dive deeper into some of its more advanced features.


I highly recommend Evernote for anyone who needs a little organization in their life. Try the free version at first if you want. If you get in the habit of using it, I bet you will eventually upgrade to the paid version 😄!

title: With each update, Evernote rises to higher levels of incompetence
body:
2025 Update:  For an app built on the promise of “capture everything,” Evernote’s use of the iPhone camera remains shockingly incapable of performing the single most basic task a modern mobile device should handle without effort: properly focusing on the thing I’m trying to photograph.

Evernote’s use of the iPhone's camera in 2025 feels like stepping back into the smartphone Stone Age — except even those early cameras at least attempted to focus.

1. Evernote Leadership Refuses to Incorporate the Most Basic Usability Features by Refusing to Fully Use the iPhone Camera APIs

It doesn’t matter whether you’re capturing a document, a receipt, a page of notes, or an object: Evernote’s camera regularly delivers blurry, unusable images. And it’s not because the device lacks capability. I’m using one of the most advanced cameras Apple has ever shipped — and yet Evernote somehow manages to turn a high-end sensor into a blurry mess.

Why? Because Evernote’s camera:
- Offers zero focusing capability
- Offers no manual controls of any kind
- Offers no ability to switch lenses
- Ignores iOS’s native camera APIs
- And constantly misfires its “auto scan” routine

Even the most trivial iOS apps — scanning apps built by one person in a weekend — manage to focus correctly. However, that's not a priority for Evernote.  Instead, they prioritize other things for development-things that pale in comparison to addressing the unbelievable shortcomings of Evernote's use of the camera.

2. Evernote's Failures to Effectively use the iPhone Camera Hinders Users Instead of Helping Them

Evernote loves to tout how their camera is designed for “fast capture.”
Let’s be clear: nothing about Evernote's use of the camera is fast. And nothing about it is useful.
Instead of a clean workflow, the user is forced into:
- Retaking scans multiple times
- Moving the phone back and forth in the hope of achieving some kind of "Kentucky windage" focus manually.
- Backing up farther than necessary, leaving the subject too small in the picture
- Wasting time in some work around using the iPhone camera app outside of Evernote, thereby cluttering the user's photo album, and requiring the user to cull through photos imported to Evernote to delete them or just live with receipts and pictures of documents amongst family photos.
- And worst of all: wasting time on a task that should take two seconds on any other app
This isn’t a minor annoyance; it’s a core function that Evernote has failed at for years, despite much earlier versions having the ability to focus the iPhone camera.

3. Evernote’s Blatant Disregard for the User

The most galling part? Evernote has received widespread feedback on this issue — repeatedly — and continues to ignore it. Users have complained across:
- App Store reviews
- Evernote forums
- Reddit
- Social media
- Support tickets
And yet Evernote remains silent.
No transparency.
No roadmap.
No acknowledgment.
No fix.
Meanwhile, competitors (including free apps!) offer:
- Superior autofocus
- Better scanning pipelines
- Cleaner UI
- Higher-quality images
- And actual support and responsiveness when something falls short in their app.
Evernote, on the other hand, seems perfectly comfortable pretending their broken camera is “good enough.”
It isn’t.

4. A Productivity App That Fails at Productivity

This is not a cosmetic issue. It’s not a “nice to have.”
A note-taking app that sells itself on capturing information must — at minimum — be able to focus the camera and capture a readable image. Evernote completly fails at these, and that demonstrates a fundamental failure of design, engineering, and customer care.

In sum, Evernote’s use of the iPhone camera is an incredibly weak link that undercuts the entire app.
If Evernote wants to call itself a modern productivity platform, it needs to fix the basics before pushing new features. In 2025, an app that can't focus the iPhone camera is unacceptable. Ignoring customer feedback makes it even worse.
Evernote users deserve a camera that works — or at the very least, a company that acknowledges when it’s failing to deliver something so basic and takes timely action to address it.

2022 Review:  
With each update, Evernote rises to higher levels of incompetence.

The organizations lacks leadership.  Each update fails to prioritize the most needed fixes.  The app can’t even focus the camera and hasn’t for well over a year.  So a core function, scanning receipts and documents, requires work arounds with the iOS camera app. Yet, the price continues to rise.  Avoid this app.  You’ll regret investing in it.  I invested in it for years, have my entire filing system in it, and I’m now planning a massive investment of time to get everything in some other application.  From this review,  I can only hope you get a sense for just how terrible this app has devolved, and choose to steer clear of it.  I’m incredibly angry and frustrated.  I feel there’s enough out there for a class action based on a breach of a services contract.

Es como una extensión de mi mente —pero con estructura, con acceso inmediato, y con esa extraña tranquilidad de saber que todo está allí, esperando por mí.

En un mundo de ruido, Evernote es orden. En un mundo de olvido, es memoria.

title: User for more than 10 years…
body:
My life is run on Evernote. More than 15 years now. I started with the free version and only upgraded with paid version a few years ago (needed more monthly storage). 

 I share my enthusiasm for Evernote with everybody, even though I’ve yet to actually utilize or optimize all of its features. I run my life and small business on it.  It’s a great product!

If I could change anything…I REALLY wish there was still a FREE VERSION to use with my clients — especially my disabled and advanced seniors,  who are less tech saavy and live on very tight fixed incomes. (they have some version of a smart phone, but not computers.)

If there was a FREE VERSION — with for smaller usage customers, I could recommend it all day every day. But a seven day trial is not enough to learn the benefits of Evernote if you’re new to such a platform or under duress of a medical condition or life crisis. 

It’s such a product existed, I (a long timely user and paying customer) could more effectively assist family, friends, and clients in time of need. I could login and quickly set them up for organized productivity to reduce their stress (and mine) if I could CREATE SHAREABLE pre and post private medical appointment NOTES and PLUS personalized reminders,  LISTS for tasks, shopping, meal prep, and KEEP updated prescription and symptom RECORDS.  Especially with the dictation and transcribe capability. As many of them have physical challenges. Not just limited tech experience. 

A special product offering for that population would be a boon to an aging, retiring, and unwell population in the U.S. and BETTER ENABLE them stay organized, maintain autonomy, get the most out of the time they have… When things take longer, and they tire more easily. Or become frustrated by complexity of life and aging or adulthood.

I truly love Evernote’s simplicity… and it’s many advanced features. It’s ideal for students, retirees, and seniors. Especially the infirmed and overwhelmed with their own independent living and medical challenges. 

Unfortunately, there no longer seems to be a FREE version for me to recommended to those I teach and assist in “the business of living”.  

I have long recommended Evernote and share my great enthusiasm for the EASE and USEFULNESS of the product. It’s just not affordable.  

A free (or almost) product that could be used by individuals I’ve described would be a boon for all of your paid customers as well.  

In my own personal experience, once you’ve used Evernote for free… You’ll never use anything else.  Eventually becoming a paying customer when circumstances improve or change. Like in my case … I couldn’t see myself using anything else and I just needed more storage.

For me, Evernote would be the ideal product for everyone of all ages, if there was a very small one time annual fee for those on limited and fixed incomes. Who are just starting off in life or struggling financially. 

Personally, I think we should be teaching elementary students to use Evernote! 

Imagine a world where everyone was much more productive, less overwhelmed by the complexities of 21st-century living, and felt a little more in control of their own personal worlds. 💪

body: This is the only application that makes copying and pasting a burden. Whenever you paste anything into Evernote, it requires a lot of annoying tedious cleanup. Just let us paste things without altering all the formatting.

title: For Seniors
body: Just record in Evernote and if you forgot, it’s all there at your fingertips!

title: Love Evernote
body: I put all my PDFs here. It’s my repository of information. Saves time and space.

title: Evernote Cultivates My Adjacent Possible
body: Many years ago I adopted Evernote after reading about the concept of the ‘adjacent possible’ in the book ‘Where Good Ideas Come From’ by Steven Johnson. Evernote is the perfect space where ideas can be stored, indexed, and revisited. It’s exactly what’s needed to help connect the ephemera of fleeting thoughts, track progress and experiment with combinations of ideas. I’d be lost without Evernote.

title: Mnemonic
body:
I am a retired teacher. My memory isn’t as good as it used to be (as one would expect) but I study my world now more than ever. With today’s easy access to an almost infinite universe of knowledge, I have, in Evernote, the greatest man-made tool I can use to aid my learning!
Thank you!

title: Could not live without it
body: Everything I need to do in one place!
I’ve been using Evernote since 2011. I have thousands of business related notes with pictures. Contact info etc. I love Evernote!
